items.title: Deere and Caterpillar Are Both Up Over 40% This Year: Take Profits or Hold On for the Ride?
items.summary: Deere and Caterpillar have each lapped the industrial sector by roughly four times over, yet the broader group never joined the party. Whether that narrowness is a warning sign or a competitive edge changes everything about what holders should do next.

items.title: What Happens To CAT Stock If Data Center Demand Cools?
items.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) stock returned 94% over the past twelve months, against 17.9% for the S&P 500, and its second quarter of 2026 was the first in company history above $20 billion of sales and revenues. One risk to that run is a quiet one. Caterpillar is adding factory capacity with data center power as a big driver, and analysts are asking whether that demand has staying power through 2030.

items.title: Meet Deere’s JD, an AI Assistant Aimed at Helping Farmers—and Its Sales
items.summary: The company is counting on quick answers and better data to attract more farmers to its smart equipment and reverse a sales slump.

items.title: Can Data Center Power Fuel CAT Stock To New Highs?
items.summary: Caterpillar (CAT) has almost doubled over the past year, gaining 96.3% while the S&P 500 returned 19.1%. Deere and Cummins each gained about 43%. The broader machinery cycle carried Caterpillar part of the way, but enthusiasm around power generation drove the premium. The gap to the stock's 52-week high is what a buyer now has to price against those expectations.

items.title: America Leans on Fusion Breakthroughs to Turbocharge Its Nuclear Weapon Arsenal
items.summary: ALBUQUERQUE, N.M.—On an expanse of desert here between a Netflix studio and self-storage facility, construction is under way on a fusion plant meant to help America win an escalating nuclear-arms race.  Testing with fusion reactors helps ensure America’s nuclear weapons still work after decades in storage, components are reliable and that new designs will have the desired effect, without resuming the explosive nuclear tests of decades prior.  At the Albuquerque groundbreaking ceremony, the site was mostly dirt, punctuated by a pair of Deere excavators holding up an American flag.
